_what: Every version of this dataset that has been DEPOSITED under a DOI. Files of a deposited version are FROZEN: Zenodo lets metadata be edited after publication, never files.
_why_this_file_exists: It was a Python literal in scripts/build_release.py, and twice in two days the just-deposited version was not added to it, so the freeze guard could not fire and overwrote deposited artefacts. 1.1.0 on 17 Nov and 1.2.0 on 18 Nov, the second time one day after the first was recorded as a lesson. A literal in a script is edited by whoever remembers; a file named `deposited.json` that both scripts read, and that preflight refuses to let fall out of step, is edited because something checks it.
_read_by: scripts/build_release.py -- refuses to rebuild a version listed here if the bytes would change
scripts/preflight_deposit.py -- refuses to prepare a deposit for a version already listed here, and refuses if a listed version's artefacts have drifted
_the_rule: ADD A VERSION HERE IMMEDIATELY AFTER PUBLISHING IT, in the same commit that records the deposit. Not later.

1.0.0.note: Deposited before the deposited-* tag convention existed. Its descriptor went up WITHOUT the DOIs, uncorrectably, because the DOI was filled in after publication and deposited files are frozen. That is why the reserve-first rule exists.

1.4.0.doi_note: THE VERSION DOI WAS NEVER REGISTERED WITH DATACITE, AND THIS IS THE ONLY VERSION FOR WHICH THAT IS TRUE. The record is published and live, state done, all five files present, and the concept DOI resolves to it -- but doi.org returns 404, api.datacite.org/dois returns 404 and the handle API returns responseCode 100. Re-checked 20 Nov 2026, two days after publication, unchanged. CONTROL THAT MAKES IT A ONE-OFF: v1.3.0 was published 2 h 26 min earlier the same day (10:54:21 against 13:20:37 UTC) from the same account by the same workflow and registered correctly, as did v1.0.0, v1.1.0, v1.2.0 and the concept DOI -- all 302 at doi.org and 200 at DataCite on 20 Nov 2026. So this is a failed registration call on Zenodo's side, not an account or workflow fault, and it CANNOT BE REPAIRED FROM THIS REPOSITORY: registration is Zenodo's action. The request to send is correspondence/2026-11-20_zenodo_support_request.md. HOW IT WAS FOUND, WHICH IS THE PART TO REMEMBER: an external correspondent could not open a DOI he had been sent. The procedure verified the CONCEPT DOI after publication and never the VERSION DOI -- the one that goes into a citation. That check is now step 7 of the deposit procedure. CITE THE RECORD URL, https://zenodo.org/records/24342313, until this is registered.

1.5.0.metadata_edited: 2026-11-20T11:57:54Z -- THE RECORD'S DESCRIPTION WAS CORRECTED IN PLACE, AFTER PUBLICATION, AND IT NOW DELIBERATELY DISAGREES WITH THE DATA_DESCRIPTOR.md FROZEN INSIDE THE SAME RECORD. Reason: the deposited descriptor attributes the minimum-attainable-p exclusion rule to Tarone RE (1990). Reading that paper on 20 Nov showed the attribution is wrong -- its own introduction credits Gart, Chu & Tarone (1979) J Natl Cancer Inst 62:957-974 and Mantel (1980) Biometrics 36:381-399, the latter attributing the remark to John Tukey, while Tarone 1990's own contribution is a sharper multiplicity correction this project does not use. Files are frozen; metadata is not. The corrected description states in plain words that the deposited file carries the superseded wording, so a reader meeting the disagreement is told why rather than left to guess. || VERIFIED AFTER THE EDIT: stored description byte-identical to release/zenodo_description_v1.5.0.snippet.html (whitespace-normalised), zero escaped tags, DOI and version unchanged, all five file md5s unchanged, additional_descriptions still empty. || AND A PROCESS NOTE WORTH KEEPING: the first attempt did not take. The form accepted the paste and the live record did not change -- `updated` stayed equal to `created` to within 0.26 s. On Zenodo's UI a metadata edit must be PUBLISHED, not only saved; a saved-but-unpublished draft looks correct in the form and is invisible to everyone else. THE CHECK THAT CATCHES IT IS `updated` MOVING, not the form's appearance. Third instance this week of: a form displaying a change is not a published change. || Full reading: reports/tarone_1990_read_2026-11-20.md.

_concept_doi_note: Resolves to the latest version. It is the cheapest check that a new version really went live: if it still resolves to the previous one, the new one is not published, whatever the form displayed.
